documents.title: Pituitary tumor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. I wanted to let you know before the letter gets to you. I told the endocrinologist on Monday about my headaches and that my period stopped last fall and there's been milky stuff from both breasts. They did a blood test and an MRI the same week, it's a pituitary tumor that makes prolactin. They said it's not cancer and a pill usually shrinks it. I started cabergoline, one pill twice a week. Honestly kind of freaked out. Is there anything I should do from your end?

documents.title: RE: Pituitary tumor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm sorry this was a scary week. A prolactin-secreting pituitary tumor is one of the most treatable tumors there is, and cabergoline is the standard first treatment; most people do very well on it. Endocrinology will lead this. Take it with food at night if it makes you queasy. I've added it to your med list. Let's talk more at your physical in July, and call sooner if the headaches get worse or your vision changes.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology clinic, follow-up visit 5/9/2022 (letter delayed).

Judith returns about seven months after her first visit, now taking levothyroxine reliably. New since then: roughly six months of headaches that are getting worse, milky discharge from both nipples, and no menses for more than eight months. She has never been pregnant. She does not notice vision problems but says small print has become harder to read.

Exam: confrontation fields show a bitemporal deficit.

Results: prolactin 210 ng/mL. TSH and free T4 normal on the current dose. Pituitary MRI: a 1.7 cm mass in the sella that reaches and presses on the optic chiasm.

Assessment: prolactin-secreting pituitary macroadenoma with chiasmal contact; hypothyroidism now controlled.

Plan: cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly. Repeat prolactin in about 3 months and pituitary MRI after a year of treatment. Call for any sudden severe headache or worsening vision. Continue levothyroxine 125 mcg.

Allergies on file: penicillin, sulfa.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology, satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.
reports.conclusion: NILM; HPV negative. Co-test in 5 years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46F, annual.

Interval: endocrinology found a prolactinoma in May (1.7 cm, touching the chiasm), on cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly since. Headaches much less. Discharge slowing down. No period yet. Taking levothyroxine daily with the pillbox, energy better, weight down a little to 72. Asthma steady, one controller puff BID.

Exam: NAD. Thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Breasts: no masses, no expressible discharge today. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected. Joints no swelling.

A/P
- Prolactinoma, improving symptomatically on cabergoline; endocrine following with prolactin and a repeat MRI.
- Hypothyroidism, controlled.
- Asthma, controlled.
- HM: Pap/HPV today. CBC, CMP, lipids. Mammogram ordered. Colonoscopy 2021 normal. Flu in fall. PHQ-9 3.
Back in a year, or sooner.

documents.body: Pap and HPV test negative, so no Pap needed for five years. Blood counts, chemistries and cholesterol are all normal.

documents.title: Office Visit - Joint Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: hands and knees hurting.

HPI: Since around April her finger joints ache and are stiff on waking, it takes over an hour before she can type properly. Over the summer it spread to both wrists and now both knees. No rash, no fevers, no recent illness, no diarrhea, no urinary symptoms, no eye flare. Aunt on mother's side has RA, sister has lupus.

Exam: Swelling and tenderness over the MCPs and PIPs of both hands, symmetric. Wrists tender. Both knees warm with a small effusion, mild. No nodules. Skin clear, no psoriasis. Eyes white.

Assessment: symmetric inflammatory small-joint polyarthritis with knee involvement, 5 months.

Plan: ESR, CRP, RF, anti-CCP, ANA today with CBC and CMP. Referring to rheumatology.

documents.title: Your joint labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your inflammation markers are up (sed rate 50, CRP 25), which fits with what we saw in your joints. The rheumatoid factor, CCP antibody and ANA tests are negative; that doesn't rule out rheumatoid arthritis, since some people test negative. Blood counts and kidney/liver tests are normal. Rheumatology has your referral and these results.

documents.title: RE: Your joint labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. They gave me Oct 25, earliest they had. Is it ok to wait?

documents.title: RE: Your joint labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that's fine. Put yourself on their cancellation list.

medications.sig: Take 8 tablets (20 mg) by mouth once a week on the same day

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Visit 10/25/2022.

Ms. Rosenblum, 46, sent for joint pain. Six months of pain and morning stiffness lasting more than an hour, beginning in the fingers and moving to the wrists and then the knees. No recent infections, GI or GU symptoms. Background of hypothyroidism and a prolactinoma on cabergoline; asthma.

Exam: both hands with swollen, tender PIP and MCP joints; both knees with mild synovitis.

Labs (drawn by PCP 9/20): ESR 50 mm/hr, CRP 25 mg/L, RF negative, anti-CCP negative, ANA negative.

Impression: seronegative rheumatoid arthritis, active.

Plan:
- Methotrexate 20 mg orally once weekly, with folic acid 1 mg daily.
- No alcohol beyond an occasional glass; she drinks little.
- CBC with CMP every 4 weeks for 2 months, then every 3 months. Her PCP's lab is fine; please forward results.
- Inactivated vaccines encouraged, including pneumococcal.
- Return 3 months.
Allergies: PCN, sulfonamides.

documents.title: Nurse Visit

documents.body: Labs for rheumatology (CBC, CMP, 2 wks into weekly methotrexate). Flu vaccine L deltoid, PCV20 R deltoid per PCP order since she's starting immunosuppression. No prior reactions. Pt says methotrexate day is Sunday, a little tired the next day but ok. Observed, no reaction.

Hands worse again for ~3 months. Stiff fingers in the morning, can't open jars, dull ache in both wrists all day. Ring feels tight. Tingling in the palms that comes and goes. On MTX 20 weekly since late October; she feels it's slipped lately.

Exam: puffy over the MCPs, tender at the wrists, grip a little weak. Sensation grossly intact.

documents.title: Orthopedics - Hand
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics and sports medicine group, hand clinic. DOS 4/26/2023.

47 y/o F with RA (rheumatology, on methotrexate) and earlier hand numbness evaluations. Three months of increasing finger stiffness, trouble with jars, steady dull ache at both wrists. Worst in the morning, makes dressing slow, loosens somewhat as the day goes on. Wedding ring is tighter. Occasional palm tingling.

Exam: swelling with tenderness at the 2nd and 3rd MCPs, both hands. Wrist flexion limited by pain. Tinel and Phalen maneuvers reproduce her paresthesias bilaterally.
Recent labs: normocytic anemia and an elevated CRP.

Impression: bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome in the setting of active RA synovitis.
Plan: prefabricated neutral wrist splints at night, both sides. MCP synovitis back to her rheumatologist. Return as needed.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

documents.title: Good news from endo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Endo appointment today. The MRI from last week shows the tumor is smaller and not touching the optic nerve anymore, and my prolactin is normal. Staying on the same cabergoline, see them in a year. Also the wrist splints at night are helping some.

documents.title: RE: Good news from endo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's exactly what we hoped for. Glad the splints help. See you in July.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual visit.

Since last year: RA diagnosed in October (seronegative), on methotrexate 20 weekly and folic acid. Bilateral carpal tunnel per ortho in April, night splints help. Prolactinoma smaller on repeat MRI, prolactin normal per endo, same cabergoline. Thyroid fine. Asthma ok.

Feels her hands are the best they've been in a year; rheum says the flare settled.

Exam: BMI ~27. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Hands with minimal MCP puffiness, no synovitis of the knees today. Skin and mouth normal.

Plan:
- CBC/CMP for MTX, TSH, lipids today. April Hgb was 11.4, recheck.
- Shingrix #1 today given immunosuppression; #2 in 2 to 6 months.
- Mammogram ordered. Pap next due 2027.
- PHQ-2 1.
1 yr, or sooner.

events.reason: Right ear hearing loss and dizziness

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For about 5 months she's had trouble hearing on the phone with her right ear, now switches to the left. Spells of the room spinning lasting minutes to an hour, a couple a month, no trigger she can find. Every so often the right side of her face feels numb. No ear pain or drainage. No new meds, nothing ototoxic.
O: Ear canals and TMs normal both sides. No nystagmus at rest. Face symmetric, strength normal.
A: Asymmetric right-sided hearing loss with episodic vertigo and right facial numbness.
P: ENT referral, they'll do audiometry. Return or ED for sudden worsening, weakness or severe headache. Shingrix #2 and flu shot today.

reports.text: Pure-tone audiometry with speech testing. Left ear: hearing within normal limits. Right ear: sensorineural hearing loss. Tympanograms type A both ears.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology group. Seen 10/25/2023.

47-year-old woman (hypothyroidism, prolactinoma, rheumatoid arthritis, carpal tunnel syndrome) with six months of progressively worse hearing in the right ear and episodes of vertigo, plus intermittent numbness of the right face. No otalgia, otorrhea or ototoxic exposures.

Exam: Weber lateralizes to the left. Rinne positive (air better than bone) on both sides. Right corneal reflex and right facial sensation are decreased.
Audiometry: right sensorineural hearing loss.

Impression: asymmetric right SNHL with vertigo and trigeminal sensory signs; retrocochlear lesion must be excluded.
Plan: MRI brain with gadolinium, internal auditory canal protocol. Will call her with results.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa drugs.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: MRI brain without and with gadolinium, including thin-section imaging of the internal auditory canals. A 1.5 cm enhancing extra-axial mass sits at the right cerebellopontine angle and extends into the right internal auditory canal; no hydrocephalus. Left IAC normal. Small known pituitary adenoma within the sella, clear of the optic chiasm. Brain parenchyma otherwise normal; no acute infarct or hemorrhage.
reports.conclusion: Right cerebellopontine angle/internal auditory canal mass, 1.5 cm, consistent with vestibular schwannoma. Known small pituitary adenoma.

documents.title: Imaging Report Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: MRI brain report from outside imaging center (ordered by ENT) received and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Ear MRI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ENT called. They said it's an acoustic neuroma on the right, about 1.5 cm, benign. Their plan is to watch it and repeat the MRI in 6 months. I didn't really think of questions on the phone. Is watching it normal?

documents.title: RE: Ear MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I saw the report too. Yes, for a benign tumor of this size, watching it with repeat scans is a common and reasonable plan, because many of them grow very slowly or not at all. If it grows, there are good treatments. Write your questions down for the ENT follow-up, and let them or me know right away about sudden hearing loss, worse balance, facial weakness or bad headaches.
